meta.title: Step 5E Pilot — Remaining Geometry Capabilities (construction-lab 1.6.0)
meta.subject: Mathematics (NaCCA Primary/JHS & Cambridge IGCSE 0580)
meta.topic: Geometry Extensions v1.6.0 Verification (12 slides: Cube Nets, Circle Theorems, Loci & Regions)

slides.title: 1. Primary Cube Net — Build a Valid Cross Net
onScreenText: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges, and 8 vertices
Not every arrangement of 6 squares folds into a cube

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#eef2ff"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#312e81">1. Cube Nets & 3D Foldability</text></svg>

narration.script: Select 6 connected squares on the grid and test whether they fold into a closed cube without overlapping faces.

keyIdeas: There are exactly 11 distinct valid cube nets (up to rotation and reflection).

commonMisconceptions: Any 6 connected squares fold into a cube

interactive.title: Test & Build a Valid Cube Net
interactive.instructions: Test this classic cross net, then try rearranging squares to discover other valid nets!
interactive.fallbackText: Classic cross net (6 faces) folds cleanly into a cube.

slides.title: 2. Primary Cuboid — Faces, Edges, Vertices & Surface Area
slides.purpose: Explore cuboid SA = 2(lw + lh + wh) and volume.

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#f0fdf4"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#14532d">2. Cuboid Surface Area & Volume</text></svg>

narration.script: Inspect the cuboid dimensions 4 by 3 by 2 and build a valid 6-face net.

keyIdeas: Surface area sums all 6 rectangular faces; volume multiplies length × width × height.

interactive.title: Cuboid Metrics & Net Builder
interactive.instructions: Inspect the 4×3×2 cuboid reference metrics and construct a valid 6-face cube net.
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Cuboid surface area and net builder
interactive.fallbackText: 4×3×2 cuboid: 6 faces, 12 edges, 8 vertices, SA=52, V=24.

slides.title: 3. IGCSE Alternate Segment Theorem
slides.purpose: Cambridge 0580 tangent-chord angle equals angle in the alternate segment.
onScreenText: Angle between tangent and chord = inscribed angle in the alternate segment

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#eff6ff"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#1e3a8a">3. Alternate Segment Theorem</text></svg>

narration.script: Move point P in the alternate segment and verify that the inscribed angle equals the tangent-chord angle.

keyIdeas: Visual exploration builds intuition; formal proof uses tangent ⊥ radius and angle at centre.

commonMisconceptions: Matching the angle in the same segment instead of alternate

circleTheorem.targetPrompt: Enter the inscribed angle ∠APB (equal to the tangent-chord angle in the alternate segment).

interactive.title: Alternate Segment Theorem Explorer
interactive.instructions: Observe the tangent-chord angle and verify ∠APB.
interactive.fallbackText: Chord spanning 120° gives inscribed angle 60° = tangent-chord angle 60°.

slides.title: 4. IGCSE Equal Tangents from an External Point
slides.purpose: Cambridge 0580 two tangents from external point E have equal length and form 90° with radii.

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#faf5ff"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#581c87">4. Equal Tangents from External Point</text></svg>

narration.script: When E is at distance 2R from O, central angle T1OT2 is 120 degrees. Find angle T1ET2.

keyIdeas: Quadrilateral OT₁ET₂ has two 90° angles, so ∠T₁ET₂ = 180° − 120° = 60°.

interactive.title: Equal Tangents from External Point E

slides.title: 5. IGCSE Perpendicular from Centre Bisects Chord
slides.purpose: Perpendicular from centre O to chord AB meets midpoint M at 90°.

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#f0fdfa"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#134e4a">5. Chord Perpendicular Bisector</text></svg>

narration.script: Verify the angle formed between radius segment OM and chord AB at midpoint M.

slides.title: 6. Locus at Fixed Distance from a Straight Line
slides.purpose: Points at distance 2 from the x-axis.
onScreenText: Locus at fixed distance d from an infinite line is TWO parallel lines

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#fff7ed"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#9a3412">6. Locus at Fixed Distance from a Line</text></svg>

narration.script: Enter coordinates of a point at exact distance 2 units from the horizontal road along the x-axis.

keyIdeas: Both y = +2 and y = −2 satisfy distance 2 from y = 0.

commonMisconceptions: Only drawing one side of the line

interactive.targetPrompt: Enter a point (x, y) at exact distance 2 from the x-axis.
interactive.title: Locus: Distance 2 from a Straight Road
interactive.instructions: Test a point (x, y) lying on the locus.
interactive.fallbackText: Any point with y = 2 or y = −2 (e.g. (0, 2)).

slides.title: 7. Locus Around a Finite Line Segment (Endpoint Arcs)
slides.purpose: Stadium locus around finite fence AB from (0,0) to (4,0) at distance 2.
onScreenText: Around a finite segment, endpoints have semicircular arcs of radius d!

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#eff6ff"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#1e3a8a">7. Locus Around a Finite Segment</text></svg>

narration.script: Find a point on the semicircular endpoint arc at distance 2 from the end of fence AB.

keyIdeas: Point (6, 0) lies on the right endpoint semicircle at distance 2 from B(4, 0).

commonMisconceptions: Drawing square corners instead of semicircular arcs

interactive.targetPrompt: Enter a point (x, y) at exact distance 2 from finite segment (0,0)–(4,0) (e.g. endpoint arc (6, 0)).
interactive.title: Locus Around a School Garden Fence
interactive.instructions: Test a point on the boundary locus including endpoint arcs.
interactive.accessibilityLabel: Finite segment locus with endpoint arcs
interactive.fallbackText: (6, 0), (-2, 0), or (2, 2) lie at exact distance 2 from segment (0,0)-(4,0).

slides.title: 8. Equidistant from Two Intersecting Lines
slides.purpose: Internal and external angle bisectors of x-axis and y-axis.
onScreenText: Equidistant from two intersecting lines = BOTH perpendicular angle bisectors (y = x and y = −x)

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#f5f3ff"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#4c1d95">8. Equidistant from Intersecting Lines</text></svg>

narration.script: Test a point equidistant from both coordinate axes.

keyIdeas: Both y = x and y = −x are equidistant from the x-axis and y-axis.

interactive.targetPrompt: Enter a point (x, y) equidistant from both the x-axis and y-axis (e.g. (3, 3) or (-2, 2)).
interactive.title: Equidistant from Two Intersecting Roads
interactive.instructions: Test a point on either angle bisector.

slides.title: 9. Equidistant from Two Parallel Lines
onScreenText: Equidistant from y = 0 and y = 6 is the midline y = 3

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#ecfeff"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#155e75">9. Equidistant from Parallel Lines</text></svg>

narration.script: Find a point halfway between parallel lines y = 0 and y = 6.

keyIdeas: The locus is the single parallel midline y = 3.

commonMisconceptions: Choosing a point outside the strip

interactive.targetPrompt: Enter a point (x, y) equidistant from parallel walls y = 0 and y = 6.
interactive.title: Midline Between Two Parallel Walls
interactive.instructions: Test a point on the midline.

slides.title: 10. Combined Locus Feasible Region (Ghana Water Borehole Siting)
slides.purpose: Intersection of distance <= 4 from Village A(0,0) AND closer to A(0,0) than B(6,0).
onScreenText: Constraint 1: within 4 km of Village A(0,0)
Constraint 2: closer to A(0,0) than B(6,0)

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#f0fdf4"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#14532d">10. Combined Locus Feasible Region</text></svg>

narration.script: Find a valid borehole coordinate within 4 units of A(0,0) and closer to A than B(6,0).

keyIdeas: Feasible regions intersect multiple inequality constraints.

interactive.targetPrompt: Enter a point (x, y) within distance 4 of A(0,0) AND closer to A(0,0) than B(6,0) (e.g. (1, 1)).
interactive.title: Siting a Community Borehole (Combined Loci)
interactive.instructions: Test coordinates inside the feasible region.
interactive.fallbackText: (1, 1) has distance 1.41 <= 4 from A and is closer to A than B(6,0).

slides.title: 11. Invalid Hexomino vs Valid Cube Net
slides.purpose: Discover why a 2×3 block of 6 squares cannot fold into a cube.
onScreenText: A 2×3 rectangle of 6 squares fails to fold into a cube — faces collide!

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#fef2f2"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#991b1b">11. Valid vs Invalid Cube Nets</text></svg>

narration.script: Test this 2 by 3 hexomino to see why it fails, then modify it into a valid cube net!

keyIdeas: No valid cube net can contain a 2×2 square of 4 faces.

interactive.title: Fix an Invalid 2×3 Hexomino into a Valid Cube Net
interactive.instructions: Click Test 3D Foldability to see the overlap error, then move squares to form a valid cube net.
interactive.fallbackText: 2×3 hexomino has overlapping folded faces; moving squares into a cross or 1-4-1 net succeeds.

slides.title: 12. Backward-Compatible Step 4F Compass Construction (Angle Bisector)
slides.purpose: Confirm existing 1.3.0 compass-straightedge activities remain 100% compatible in 1.6.0.
onScreenText: All existing Step 4F geometry activities continue unchanged

visual.svgCode: <svg viewBox="0 0 800 450" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg"><rect width="800" height="450" fill="#f8fafc"/><text x="400" y="225" text-anchor="middle" font-family="sans-serif" font-size="30" font-weight="bold" fill="#0f172a">12. Step 4F Compatibility — Angle Bisector</text></svg>

narration.script: Construct the angle bisector of ∠AOB using compass arcs.

keyIdeas: Every point on an angle bisector is equidistant from both rays.

interactive.title: Construct the Angle Bisector of ∠AOB
interactive.instructions: Draw the bisector ray from O(0,0) through (4,4).
interactive.fallbackText: Bisector of 90° angle ∠AOB is the ray y = x.
